input:
You are pawn_f2, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 12. the team planned f3 (pawn_f2), but queen_d1 (greed) sent Qxa4 instead, and that move was played, costing 42 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 7. the team planned h3 (pawn_h2), but pawn_h2 (amnesia) sent h4 instead, and that move was played, costing 88 centipawns.
- On move 9. the team planned d3 (pawn_d2), but pawn_d2 (amnesia) sent d4 instead, and that move was played, costing 67 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send your piece's move only if it is the exact move named in the plan (matching piece and destination square); if the plan names a different piece, stay silent, and never replace the planned move with a capture or a retreat unless the team has approved that move in chat.
- Before sending your piece's move, write the exact planned move (piece and destination square) in chat and copy it character for character into your send, and if what you are about to send differs in any way from the plan, including a capture or a retreat when your piece is threatened, do not send it and instead post the difference in chat and wait for team approval.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "After the plan is posted, the agent whose piece is named in the plan must reply in chat with the planned move and wait for one other agent to confirm it matches the plan before sending, and every other agent must send nothing, since a piece not named in the plan has no move to send.", "covers": ["greed", "amnesia", "panic"]}
